mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy accommodates growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate rise above 0.5% signals imminent monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and real disposable income (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand, driving corporate revenue growth and positive equity returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST and RSAFS both rising) fails to produce positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 50% of instances over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Payroll growth exceeding 0.5% monthly (PAYEMS) in a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals labor market strength supporting consumer spending, generating positive 5-day SPX returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% monthly over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Positive quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, supporting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth exceeds 0.5% quarterly over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100 indicates weakening supply chain activity, signaling potential recession and negative equity returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is below 100 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates delayed monetary tightening, generating positive 5-day SPX returns as markets anticipate accommodative policy.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS low and CPIAUCSL rising) fails to produce positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 50% of instances over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) combined with strong job growth (PAYEMS > 0.3% monthly) signals wage pressure and consumer spending strength, driving positive 20-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% and PAYEMS rises > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when both UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.3% monthly over any 3-year rolling window.
